A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DuetServe, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. The comparison includes v2's Appendices A and B; v1 has no appendices. Material relocated from v1's main text is identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPU profiling, serving benchmarks on three workload traces, multi-GPU measurements and component analyses in Sections 3 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original measurements and adds synthetic workload results in Appendix A and an eight-GPU comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the decode allocation search from range(1, S+1, 2) to range(2, S+1, 2), using even SM counts consistent with two-SM TPC granularity. This corrects the reported procedure without establishing an implementation change. The predictor, optimization objective and look-ahead execution mechanism otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds controlled synthetic serving scenarios with 4,096 input tokens and 64, 1,024 or 2,048 output tokens, testing different prefill/decode balances. The three real-world traces and application domain remain unchanged. The larger model and GPU configuration are setting changes under E3.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain vLLM, SGLang-Default, SGLang-Chunked, Dynamo and the same static-partition controls. The added experiments reuse vLLM and Dynamo; newly cited systems such as DeepSpeed-FastGen are not evaluated. Dynamo's larger configuration and runtime replanning are added experimental settings.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds an eight-H100 experiment using Qwen3-32B on Azure-Conv at QPS 24, comparing DuetServe TP=8 with Dynamo initialized at 4P+4D and allowed to reconfigure. It also reports average GPU utilization. Appendix A adds fixed-input, varying-output tests at maximum serving capacity. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the original settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a three-setting workload-sensitivity study and reports that calibrating decode-latency predictions produced no noticeable performance improvement. The existing roofline-accuracy, static-partition and execution-trace analyses are retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. The additional mean latency and utilization measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation plots retain their results. New Table 2 reports throughput gains of 1.28×, 1.11× and 1.04× as output length increases. New Table 3 reports Dynamo versus DuetServe throughput of 5.69 versus 8.02 req/s and TTFT of 110.2 versus 58.9 seconds, but TBT of 23.1 versus 104.7 ms. These are substantial additional results under new conditions, not improvements over v1's measurements.

T1.justification: The roofline cost expressions, ring-AllReduce formulation and constrained throughput objective retain their mathematical substance. Changes to element-size and bandwidth symbols standardize notation, and KV-cache concatenation remains described in prose after its displayed equation is removed. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same three central components, adaptive intra-GPU isolation claim and up-to-1.3× throughput claim. The rewritten conclusion restates these contributions; the additional appendix evidence does not redefine the headline claims.

C2.justification: Appendices A and B substantially expand interpretation and limitations: asymmetric consequences of predictor overestimation versus underestimation, diminishing benefits for decode-heavy workloads, whole-GPU reconfiguration costs, single-node evaluation limits, missing multi-node communication modeling, saturation-related SLO failures and untested heterogeneity. These meaningfully qualify and explain the retained claims.

D1.justification: The new experiments document workload lengths and cluster configuration, including Dynamo's initial 4P+4D allocation, planner use and model reload, warm-up and KV-cache rebuilding during role changes. The original implementation description and software versions remain unchanged, and no new DuetServe code-access information is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds DeepSpeed-FastGen, references on disaggregation tradeoffs, MimicNet and TACOS, removes the original FlashAttention citation, and sharpens positioning against whole-GPU disaggregation. Drift and MuxWise share the same cited arXiv identifier and are matched as renamed work; publication updates are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The introduction and parts of the motivation are substantially compressed and rewritten. Section 5.4 moves into Appendix A, Appendix B establishes a dedicated discussion structure, and the related-work and conclusion narratives are revised. Author/front-matter information, an impact statement and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the first-page abstract layout, relocates the overview diagram, moves the ablation displays into single-column appendices and adds Tables 2 and 3. Figure 10 is enlarged and annotated to identify dispatch activity, streams and execution modes. The original plotted data are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The synthetic sweep clarifies when benefits diminish, and the eight-GPU comparison addresses the restricted two-GPU disaggregation setup in v1. Expanded limitations and the annotated execution trace improve interpretation. These are useful but bounded extensions: the larger comparison covers one setting and shows higher TBT alongside better throughput and TTFT, supporting a modest overall quality improvement.
